target_customer: Governments, defence and intelligence agencies, and satellite operators that need images of other spacecraft
problem: Operators and defence agencies lack independent, timely imagery of satellites in orbit, and dedicated inspector spacecraft are expensive. HEO adds software to existing Earth observation satellites so they can image other objects as they pass close.
business_model: Imagery and analytics sold to government and operator customers, delivered through partner satellites hosting HEO software

founders.name: Will Crowe
education: PhD in Aerospace Engineering (astrodynamics of spacecraft swarms near asteroids)
founders.background_notes: YC page says he won the Space Generation Advisory Council Move an Asteroid award in 2015.

founders.name: Hiranya Jayakody
education: PhD in mechatronics engineering, UNSW Sydney
Bachelor in electronics engineering, University of Peradeniya, Sri Lanka
founders.background_notes: Researched computer vision and machine learning for agriculture and control of aerial vehicles and space robots, per YC page.

competitors.name: SCOUT Space
competitors.what: In-space inspection and situational awareness sensors, announced a hosted payload SSA mission with Orbit Fab
competitors.traction_then: Announced a first commercial in-space SSA demonstration mission

technical_complexity.rationale: Imaging fast-moving objects from existing third-party satellites needs onboard software, tasking and image processing for non-Earth targets, with partner satellite access.

defensibility.rationale: Partnerships with satellite owners and a growing image dataset help, but the approach relies on partner access and rivals could build inspector satellites.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source found showing incumbents copying or buying the wedge; HEO raised a Series A in 2023.

market_need_then: Growing government interest in space domain awareness and rising numbers of satellites around 2021, though no dated source on demand figures was opened.

branding.name_origin: Legal name is High Earth Orbit Robotics Pty Ltd, shortened to HEO; a source stating why was not found.

identity.logo: White and blue logo versions per the company site
identity.voice_and_tone: Technical and defence oriented, positioned around non-Earth imaging

branding.brand_signature: Non-Earth imaging as a coined category phrase

rebrands.why: Not stated; the company now uses HEO and domain heospace.com, date unknown

brand_strength.rationale: Little press on the brand itself found; a niche B2B and defence audience.

outcome_analysis: HEO stayed active after YC Summer 2021, raising a roughly 3 million dollar seed in September 2021 and an AUD 12 million Series A led by AirTree in August 2023. Founders with aerospace and robotics PhDs fit a defence-driven space awareness market, and the software-on-existing-satellites approach kept hardware cost low. The company site also references a later US$25 million raise that was not verified with a dated source.
notes: Series A reported as AUD 12m by company release and AVCJ; SpaceNews and ZoomInfo say 8 million (USD). Amount_usd left null for the Series A because of the currency conflict. Seed amount of 3m comes from an editor's note in Startup Daily, currency unstated. A US$25M raise appears on the company site and a 26.4M Series B in an aggregator, both unverified. Outcome search found no acquisition, layoffs or shutdown news.
